parsed_answer.content: Redis HyperLogLog is a probabilistic data structure designed to estimate the cardinality of a massive dataset—the number of unique elements—with extreme memory efficiency. In high-scale distributed systems, tracking unique visitors, distinct IP addresses, or unique event IDs across billions of records using a standard Set would consume gigabytes of RAM, leading to inevitable OOM (Out of Memory) errors. HyperLogLog solves this by leveraging the Flajolet-Martin algorithm, which uses the properties of hash functions to observe the maximum number of leading zeros in a binary sequence. By tracking only these patterns, it provides an estimate with a standard error of less than 1% while consuming a fixed, tiny memory footprint of approximately 12KB, regardless of whether you are counting one thousand or one billion unique items.

items: The algorithm works by hashing the input element into a 64-bit integer, then splitting this hash into two parts: a bucket index (determined by the first few bits) and a value (the position of the leftmost '1' bit in the remaining bits).
It maintains an array of 16,384 registers, each 6 bits wide. Each register stores the maximum number of leading zeros observed for the inputs mapped to that specific bucket.
The final cardinality is calculated using the harmonic mean of these registers, which effectively dampens the impact of outliers and provides a statistically robust estimate.

HyperLogLog is strictly a write-only estimation structure; you cannot retrieve the original elements, nor can you perform set intersections or differences with the same precision as standard Redis Sets.

parsed_answer.content: Senior Engineer Insight: Never use HyperLogLog if your business logic requires exact counts (e.g., financial ledger balances). The 0.81% error rate is cumulative; if you merge multiple HLL structures, the error can drift slightly. Always ensure your hash function is uniform to avoid skewing the register distribution, though Redis handles this internally with MurmurHash64.
